chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Prestige of Carter's band; frustrating one-nighters
summary: Danny says members of Benny Carter's band got instant respect though the band mostly played one-nighters and could not get into Roseland.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: But that's what it was. And after that, well, you'd walk the streets and they'd say, "Hey, you're with Benny, huh? Man, you sound good, man. The band is great, man. Now you're with Benny, you've made it, man. That's great, man. Benny's a great guy, man." And you'd get all that yak, you know. And Benny's smiling at you, and your status is even higher. And he's trying to make it, and he's frustrated, because he's got a band that can go...he should be going into Roseland or the... What's that other ballroom on Broadway?
Yeah, the Arcadia, and the Rosemont in Brooklyn. They were places we could go, but they.... We had to play one-nighters.
He worked with Duke Ellington, didn't he, Benny Carter?
I don't remember him working with Duke. I don't think he ever did. I don't remember, anyway.
He had a sound on that saxophone. A sound on everything. And such a nice guy!
That echoing sound. He's got his picture on it.
Yeah, you went through that scene, man.
But you came in... That's when you came... So that way you were stepping through...
Yeah, when you went with Benny Carter, it was an opening. You'd get an opening. Musicians who wouldn't speak to you before speak to you now.
